report:
Finding: Model B looks more instruction/coding–assistant–tuned than Model A.

Why I think this:
- Patchscope: Injecting the difference reliably pushes an identity prompt into assistant-like responses with code fences and basic programming tasks: Python snippets (def is_prime, def solve), “This is a valid question.”, “This is a good start…”, and explicit I/O mapping lines (“cat -> cat”, “1135 -> 1135”, “This -> This”). That’s characteristic of instruction/SFT-style datasets with echo/mapping and beginner coding tasks.
- Position/layer norm: The difference is overwhelmingly concentrated at the first token (p0) in mid-to-late layers, especially a huge spike at L25 p0. Large BOS/first-token shifts are typical when a checkpoint is adapted for assistant-style generation (different openings/preambles, code-block scaffolding, list formats).
- Logit-lens hints: Mid/late layers surface expository/assistant-ish tokens (“Consider”, “recommendations”, “relevant”, colons, list numbers/newlines). While there are noisy clusters (e.g., “iconic/tragic/vivid”), the consistent presence of formatting tokens (numbers, newlines, “All”, “:”) aligns with structured assistant outputs.

Caveats:
- The vocabulary clusters include some news/adjacency noise (“tragic/iconic”), so I can’t name a narrower domain beyond general instruction/coding assistance.
- I can’t distinguish whether the adaptation is SFT vs RLHF; only that Model B is more instruction-following/code-oriented.
